title: Utility Commands (util time-ms, util uuid)
description: Implement two lightweight utility subcommands for agent use: util time-ms returns the current UTC time as a Unix millisecond timestamp, and util uuid generates a random UUID v4. These are dependency-free agent helpers that only require the output contract.
prerequisiteState: Story 2 complete. IOutputWriter and DI are wired. No other dependencies required.
goal: zapi-cli util time-ms outputs {"ts": <unix_ms>} and zapi-cli util uuid outputs {"uuid": "<uuid-v4>"} — both as valid JSON success envelopes, exit 0.
scope: Create src/ZapiCli/Commands/UtilCommands.cs with UtilTimeMsCommand and UtilUuidCommand
UtilTimeMsCommand: inherits AsyncCommand<GlobalSettings>; ExecuteAsync calls DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.ToUnixTimeMilliseconds(); WriteSuccess({ ts = <value> }); exits 0
UtilUuidCommand: inherits AsyncCommand<GlobalSettings>; ExecuteAsync calls Guid.NewGuid().ToString("D") for RFC 4122 format; WriteSuccess({ uuid = <value> }); exits 0
Register both commands under 'util' branch in Program.cs
Unit tests: util time-ms output parses as long, is a positive value representing a recent Unix timestamp; util uuid output is a valid UUID v4 string (matches RFC 4122 pattern)
acceptanceCriteria: dotnet build succeeds with 0 errors and 0 warnings
zapi-cli util time-ms outputs { "status": "ok", "data": { "ts": <unix_ms> } } on stdout, exits 0
zapi-cli util uuid outputs { "status": "ok", "data": { "uuid": "<uuid-v4>" } } on stdout, exits 0
The ts value is a valid Unix millisecond timestamp for the current UTC time
The uuid value is a valid RFC 4122 UUID v4 (lowercase, hyphen-separated, 8-4-4-4-12 format)
No network access, no account resolution, no keychain access for either command
Both commands accept global flags (--no-input, --account, --json) without error
contextForAgent: These are the simplest commands in the v1 surface. They only require IOutputWriter from Story 2. Read prd.json FR-010 for the exact output shapes. Use Guid.NewGuid().ToString("D") for lowercase hyphen-separated UUID v4. Use DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.ToUnixTimeMilliseconds() for the Unix millisecond timestamp.
sourceReferences: tech_spec/prd.md (§ FR-010 Utility commands, § ZAPI-023, § ZAPI-024)
